rfm_tuples.f: Verify HTM/AFS embedded loss vs tangible common equity. Post-SVB, this is a survival-relevance check for any regional bank with -20% drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_value: HTM gross unrealized losses sum to ~$686.9M ($96.0 + $133.7 + $436.1 + $21.1) on $3.64B amortized cost — a 18.9% mark on the HTM book. Tangible common equity = book value $3.53B - goodwill+intangibles ~$1.42B = ~$2.11B. Embedded HTM+AFS loss is 48% of TCE. If forced to sell HTM at fair value, TCE would compress to ~$1.42B (-33%).

summary: SFNC is a long-tenured regional bank (Forvis Mazars auditor since 1972) with multiple MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY framing issues at YE24 that became visible in the Q1 2025 10-Q filed one week before cutoff. The headline 'credit quality remained solid' is decisively contradicted by Q1 2025 figures: nonperforming assets surged 34% sequentially to $162.3M, driven by two specific credit relationships (a $26.9M downtown St. Louis hotel classified since April 2021 and a $22.9M fast-food operator classified since June 2024) that the YE24 10-K did not call out by name despite years on the watch list. Securities-portfolio mark-to-market loss is meaningful: HTM unrealized loss of $686.9M (18.9% of amortized cost) is ~33% of tangible common equity — a post-SVB tail risk that MD&A does not foreground. Total CRE concentration sits at ~330% of RBC, above the 300% regulator guideline. Counter-signals: no going-concern language, capital ratios solid (Tier 1 leverage 9.74%), insiders did not sell into the Q1 2025 deterioration (zero Q1/Q2 2025 sales after $2.3M of routine 2024 sales), counterparty-mirror EDGAR check is clean, and FDIC call-report data exactly matches disclosed figures. The bank is honestly disclosing — full reconciliations are in the filings — but the MD&A framing is selective on credit velocity, named-credit specifics, HTM mark vs TCE, and CRE concentration ratios. Verdict tilts NEUTRAL with moderate downside lean given the credit-cycle turn evidence in the pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q.
